full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment of August 31, 2004 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2072 of 2000 making absolute the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated February 28, 2000 of the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 13 of 1995 allowing the same and thereby dis-missing the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree dated September 25, 1994 of the 2nd Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 19 of 1993 decreeing the same and thereupon directing the defendants to reinstate the plaintiff in his post with effect from September 20, 1990 within 45 days with the benefits and allowances except two increments. 

 5. The trial Court decreed the suit on the findings that there has been violation of Rule 46(2) of the service rules of WASA since from the very day of preliminary inquiry plaintiff was put under suspension and the charge-sheet was not served within 30 days as per the rules and that the appeal was not disposed of within 60 days from the date of submission of the appeal, that the inquiry report on the basis of which plaintiff was dismissed from service was violative of the provision of Rule 45(2) since Inquiry Committee was not authorized to make recommendation as to the nature and period of punishment or kind of punishment. 

 6. The defendant No. 1 i.e. WASA went on appeal. The appellate Court allowed the appeal with the findings that the charge-sheet was served on the plaintiff quite within time and regular proceeding was initiated and there was an inquiry, that charge-sheet was submitted and a Inquiry Committee was constituted and during inquiry plaintiff was given opportunity to put forward his case as against the charges brought against him and the Inquiry Committee submitted its report with the recommendation of dismissing the plaintiff from service, that on the basis of the inquiry report 2nd show cause notice was served and thereupon on completion of the procedural formalities the plaintiff was dismissed from service and lateron his appeal was rejected. The appellate Court also held that there was no violation of the provision of service rules of the WASA, that the judgment and decree of the trial Court is not based on evidence and the same is contrary to law. 

 8. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the finding that plaintiff was dismissed from service without following the procedure as provided by the service rules of the WASA employees, that the admission of guilt by the plaintiff was made having been put under pressure by the authority and that the appellate Court has not reversed the said finding upon taking into consideration the attending facts and circumstances of the case, that the WASA authority reinstated the 4 other officials who along with the plaintiff were found guilty by the Inquiry Committee and were also dismissed from service but for no reasonable cause plaintiff was not reinstated and as such the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court calls for interference since the appellate Court made the judgment in not noticing the material fact that the persons guilty of the offence as the plaintiff was found were reinstated by the authority, but refused the prayer of the plaintiff for reinstatement for no logic and on no reasonable ground.
